issues.legal_issue: The right of an inam holder to retain the difference between the full land assessment and the reduced payment is a right in an estate protected from constitutional challenge under the estate-law protection.
material_facts: The holders possessed personal inams under which they paid less than the full land assessment and retained the difference.
The challenged enactment extinguished the personal inams, made the lands liable for full land revenue, and ended the holders’ right to retain that difference.
issues.conclusion: The inams were estates, and the holders’ right to retain the difference was a right in an estate and a right or privilege in respect of land revenue. The enactment’s extinguishment or modification of that right was protected by Article 31-A.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A(1)(a) protects laws providing for the acquisition of an estate or rights in it, or the extinguishment or modification of such rights, from challenges under Articles 14, 19 and 31. Under Article 31-A(2)(a), an estate includes an inam; under Article 31-A(2)(b), rights in an estate include rights or privileges in respect of land revenue. The right also fell within section 3(5) of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, 1879. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_law and inam_tenure and holder_retained_revenue_difference and law_extinguished_or_modified_that_right

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_law: A person challenged the constitutionality of a law affecting rights held under a land tenure.
predicates.inam_tenure: The affected land tenure was an inam.
predicates.holder_retained_revenue_difference: The tenure holder paid less than the full land assessment and retained the difference.
predicates.law_extinguished_or_modified_that_right: The challenged law extinguished or modified the holder’s right to retain that difference.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a law that alters an inam holder’s right to retain revenue not paid as land assessment, the law is protected from the relevant fundamental-rights challenge.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of compensation for ending the inam holder’s right to retain the difference between the full assessment and the reduced payment does not invalidate the enactment when the enactment is protected by the estate-law protection.
material_facts: The enactment made the inam lands liable for full assessment, ending the holders’ benefit from paying a reduced amount.

The enactment provided compensation for certain lands vested in the State but expressly denied compensation for the loss of the benefit arising from the difference between the reduced payment and the full assessment.
The enactment extinguished or modified rights in inams, which the Court held were estates and rights in estates protected by Article 31-A.
issues.conclusion: The absence of compensation for the loss of the revenue difference did not make the enactment unconstitutional, because Article 31-A protected it from an attack under Article 31.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31 provided for compensation, but Article 31-A protected laws concerning the acquisition of estates or rights in them, and the extinguishment or modification of those rights, from challenges under Article 31. Section 17(5) of the Bombay Personal Inams Abolition Act, 1952, denied compensation for the loss caused by making previously exempt or partly exempt land subject to full assessment. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_law and inam_tenure and law_ended_reduced_revenue_payment and law_extinguished_or_modified_rights_in_the_tenure

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_law: A person challenged the constitutionality of a law affecting rights held under a land tenure.
predicates.inam_tenure: The affected land tenure was an inam.
predicates.law_ended_reduced_revenue_payment: The law made the land liable for full assessment and ended the holder’s reduced payment.
predicates.law_extinguished_or_modified_rights_in_t: The law extinguished or modified rights held under the inam tenure.

issues.definition: When a challenged law ends reduced revenue payment and alters rights in an inam tenure, its lack of compensation for that loss does not invalidate it.
